title: Flix Consumer Projection Map Schema
description: Maps a consumer parser's native node vocabulary onto the canonical TreeKind names in ast/treekind.json. Consumers whose parse trees already carry canonical names need no map.

consumer.description: Repository or tool this map belongs to, e.g. tree-sitter-flix.

mappings.description: Native node name -> canonical TreeKind name. Every value must exist in ast/treekind.json.

ignored.description: Native nodes that are transparent when they wrap at most one child: dropped when empty, replaced by their child when they wrap exactly one. A node may also appear in `mappings`, which is not a contradiction -- elision only fires at arity <= 1, so the two entries describe different positions. Precedence-chain grammars require this: a level like ADDITIVE_EXPR is a pass-through on every expression without a `+`, and a real binary expression when one is present. Anything neither mapped nor ignored is reported as unmapped, which is a gap rather than a decision.

notes.description: Free-form per-node rationale, keyed by native node name.

elide.description: DEPRECATED. Canonical TreeKind names this consumer legitimately does not produce, skipped when matching. Only a node with at most one child may be elided -- eliding a branching node would discard structure rather than a wrapper. Superseded by ast/transparency.json, which removes these nodes from fixtures/expected/ before any consumer sees them: doing it once, in the reference's repository, with a reason argued from the reference's own structure, is neutral in a way that doing it per consumer never was. Every entry here that names a kind ast/transparency.json already removes is dead weight and should be deleted. What remains admissible is a consumer-specific extra -- a canonical kind that consumer genuinely cannot produce but that is not transparent in the reference -- and each one is evidence about that consumer, not about the canonical tree.

flatten.description: Native grouping nodes whose children are spliced into the parent at any arity. Stronger and more dangerous than `ignored`, which only fires at arity <= 1: flattening a node that carries real structure would hide a genuine disagreement. Use only for pure grouping constructs with no counterpart in the reference, and justify each entry in `notes`.

flattenCanonical.description: DEPRECATED. Canonical TreeKind names whose children are spliced into the parent at any arity -- the mirror of `flatten`, which does the same on the consumer's side. Needed when the reference groups members the consumer makes direct children: `UsesOrImports.UseOrImportList` holds every use in one node, and `elide` cannot remove it because elision only fires at arity <= 1. Superseded by ast/transparency.json's `splice` rule for the error vocabulary, which is the one case where splicing a canonical node is a fact about the reference rather than about a consumer. Retained for consumer-specific extras; every value must exist in ast/treekind.json.
